 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

1. Petitioners file these petitions for quashing of the FIR No.47/2021 under Section 323/341/34 Indian Penal Code as also FIR No.46/2021under Section 323/354A/506/509/34 Indian Penal Code both registered at police station Mangolpuri, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Essentially, the aforesaid cross FIRs were got registered by the parties during the counselling proceedings of the matrimonial complaint.
The marriage between the Manish Aggarwal and Ritu Garg was solemnized on 17.01.2019 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child is born from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple could not live together and started living separately from each other since 21.06.2020 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 the FIR No.689/2021 was registered against the petitioners.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 27.05.2022.

sentences.text:
Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.47.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past,
present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
The said amount has already been received by respondent No.2.
The matrimonial FIR under Section 498A/406/34 Indian Penal Code has since been quashed today in W.P.(Crl) No.165/2023.

3. With the amicable settlement of matrimonial dispute, the respective complainants of aforesaid FIRs do not wish to pursue their complaints against respective petitioners as aforesaid disputes /
scuffle was essentially related to the matrimonial dispute, which has since been settled between the parties and they have parted their ways.

4. The complainant/respondent No.2 in both the cases have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the respective petitioners having left with no claim against them and they have has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned Standing Counsel and learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.
5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as respective complainants have settled all the disputes including the matrimonial dispute.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, these petitions are allowed.

Consequently, FIR No.47/2021 under Section 323/341/34 Indian Penal Code as also FIR No.46/2021under Section 323/354A/506/509/34 Indian Penal Code both registered at police station Mangolpuri, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
JANUARY 20, 2023 M Ritu Garg And Ors.
